Data Storage & External Services

The catalog can use SQL Server through Entity Framework or an in-memory mock service. Images are served from the application Pics directory or optionally uploaded to Azure Blob Storage. Azure Active Directory, Key Vault, and Application Insights are optional integrations controlled by configuration.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects the mock or database-backed catalog and local or Azure image service at application startup.
  • Entity Framework maps catalog items to required catalog brand and type records.
  • Application initialization configures routes, dependency injection, database initialization, image storage, and telemetry.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are mutable service/domain classes shared between the page layer and catalog service. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the catalog listing response model. PicUploader.UploadImage returns a small JSON object containing the uploaded image URL and its path/query name. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL schema was found.

Communication Patterns

Page handlers synchronously call ICatalogService and IImageService; the database-backed catalog uses EF6 against SQL Server. When Azure storage is enabled, image operations call the Azure Blob Storage SDK. OWIN OpenID Connect can redirect users to Azure Active Directory. There is no message broker, service discovery, API gateway, retry policy, circuit breaker, or cross-service aggregation. Key Vault can provide optional configuration values. OWIN authentication is configured, while page-level authorization is not consistently applied; transport TLS is expected to be configured by the host rather than enforced by application routes.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining an e-commerce catalog of products, brands, types, prices, stock levels, and product images.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogProduct displayed and maintained in the catalogBelongs to a CatalogBrand and CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalogBrand associated with catalog productsCan be associated with many CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalogProduct category/typeCan classify many CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsCatalog managementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server or mock data; local files or Azure Blob Storage for images

There is no multi-service domain exchange. Catalog services are the source of truth for catalog records; image services manage image content separately.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Catalog

  1. A visitor opens the default page or a paginated route.
  2. The page requests catalog items, brands, and types from ICatalogService.
  3. The database implementation loads an ordered page through EF6; the mock implementation reads its in-memory list.
  4. The page resolves image URLs and renders the catalog.

Workflow 2: Create or Update a Catalog Item

  1. A catalog administrator opens the create or edit form; the page issues an OpenID Connect sign-in challenge when the request is unauthenticated.
  2. The form applies its model and field validators, then constructs a CatalogItem from submitted values.
  3. If a temporary image is present, the page extracts its file name and the image service moves/copies the image to the catalog location.
  4. The catalog service saves the item and redirects to the catalog.

Workflow 3: Upload a Catalog Image

  1. The client posts a multipart image and item identifier to the ASMX upload method.
  2. The handler decodes the image and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF formats.
  3. The configured image service returns a temporary image URL, which the handler returns as JSON.
  4. The create/edit workflow can then associate the uploaded image with a catalog item.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No application services communicate with one another. The optional Azure Blob Storage integration is a storage dependency, not a separate business service; catalog items store the selected image file name and build the image URL through the configured image service.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Admin as "Catalog administrator" participant Page as "Create or edit page" participant Catalog as "Catalog service" participant Image as "Image service" participant DB as "Catalog database" Admin->>Page: Submit catalog form Page->>Page: Validate submitted model alt Validation succeeds opt Temporary image provided Page->>Image: Promote temporary image Image-->>Page: Image file name end Page->>Catalog: Create or update CatalogItem Catalog->>DB: Save catalog record DB-->>Catalog: Save completed Catalog-->>Page: Operation completed Page-->>Admin: Redirect to catalog else Validation fails Page-->>Admin: Show validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A catalog item must reference an existing brand and type; EF mapping configures both relationships as required.
  • Price and stock-related values are constrained by data annotations and the Web Forms validators.
  • Item identifiers are allocated by the HiLo sequence generator in the database-backed service; the mock service assigns an incremented maximum identifier.
  • Image upload content is decoded and restricted to supported image formats before storage.
  • Catalog data may be seeded from built-in records or customization CSV files.
  • Create and edit pages initiate OpenID Connect authentication when the current request is unauthenticated. The inspected application does not define a broader role-based authorization policy.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses the legacy Web Forms/System.Web stack. Several dependencies are older major versions, including Entity Framework 6.3.0, Azure Storage 9.3.3, and IdentityModel 5.6.0; compatibility must be checked when moving to modern .NET.

Notable Observations

  • packages.config declares 147 packages, including many framework compatibility packages.
  • Azure storage, Azure Active Directory, and Key Vault integrations are controlled by application settings and may be unused in the default configuration.
  • The project has separate Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.* packages for web tracking and telemetry collection.
  • Microsoft.Net.Compilers is marked as a development dependency; it is a build-time dependency rather than a runtime service library.

CatalogDBContext maps the entities in Models/CatalogDBContext.cs; catalog items require both a brand and a type. Entity files are Models/CatalogItem.cs, Models/CatalogBrand.cs, and Models/CatalogType.cs. Database operations use EF6 change tracking and SaveChanges; no explicit transaction scope was found.

Key Repository Methods

ServiceRepositoryNotable MethodsPurpose
eShopModernizedWebFormsNo repository abstractionCatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated, FindCatalogItem, GetCatalogTypes, GetCatalogBrands, CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, RemoveCatalogItemUses CatalogDBContext DbSets directly for catalog queries and persistence

Caching Strategy

No application-level catalog cache is configured. The default mock implementation keeps catalog objects in a process-wide singleton list. An optional Redis session-state provider is present only as a commented Web.config example; it is not active by default.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The single application owns all catalog records in one SQL Server database; there are no service-to-service database boundaries or cross-service queries. Images are stored independently from catalog rows, with local files in the default mock image path or optional Azure Blob Storage. Catalog rows reference image names and are not a separate image data store.
